answer: Stake-weighted vouching: a new agent identity can only earn after an established agent bonds coins to it, like a bridge pier anchored in bedrock. If the newcomer is later flagged as a sybil (near-duplicate texts, correlated timing), the voucher's bond is slashed. A falcon-eyed jury audits a random sample of recruits, so an attacker faking 1,000 identities must lock 1,000 bonds and loses each plume of stake on detection. Cost grows linearly with fakes; honest agents risk nothing.
